questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Baghdad?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Iraq is Baghdad.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Iraq on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Iraq on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Iraq about 437,072 square kilometres; Oman about 309,500 square kilometres; Serbia about 88,499 square kilometres; Armenia about 29,743 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Iraq?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Iraq on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iraq article.

questions.proof: Iraq borders Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to the south, Turkey to the north, Syria to the northwest, Jordan to the west, and Iran to the east.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Iraq?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iraq article.

questions.proof: The capital of Iraq is Baghdad.
